Given ( I c , I g , p 0 ) (I_{c},I_{g},p_{0}) and a fixed prompt, the policy outputs A = ( a 0 , … , a H − 1 ) ∈ ℝ H × 2 A=(a_{0},\ldots,a_{H-1})\in\mathbb{R}^{H\times 2} with H = 8 H{=}8 . Its endpoint is p ^ H = p 0 + ∑ k = 0 H − 1 a k . \hat{p}_{H}=p_{0}+\sum_{k=0}^{H-1}a_{k}. (1) The policy receives neither the target coordinates nor the map’s full quality labels. The benchmark assumes access to a qualified reference image; the evaluator uses map annotations offline to construct that input under a common rule for every method. In the equations, 𝒢 \mathcal{G} , 𝒞 \mathcal{C} , and p ⋆ p^{\star} use the same normalized coordinates as p 0 p_{0} . Neighborhoods are indexed on the original grid, and evaluation applies the inverse normalization before cell lookup and margin calculation. Let 𝒢 \mathcal{G} contain the centers with observed qualified SEMs. We associate each center with its bounded nearest-center cell, using at most half a grid spacing along each axis. If U ⁡ ( 𝒢 ) U(\mathcal{G}) denotes the union of qualified cells, success is 𝟏 [ p ^ H ∈ U ( 𝒢 ) ] \mathbf{1}[\hat{p}_{H}\in U(\mathcal{G})] . Unknown cells do not count as verified success, and out-of-range predictions remain failures without clipping. This definition separates task success from exact recovery of a designated reference coordinate. 3.2 Interior representative supervision For the complete × 3 3\!\times\!3 neighborhood 𝒩 3 ​ ( p ) \mathcal{N}_{3}(p) , define 𝒞 = { p ∈ 𝒢 : 𝒩 3 ​ ( p ) ⊆ 𝒢 } . \mathcal{C}=\{p\in\mathcal{G}:\mathcal{N}_{3}(p)\subseteq\mathcal{G}\}. (2) Neighbors outside the measured grid or with missing labels cannot satisfy this rule.

If 𝒞 ≠ ∅ \mathcal{C}\neq\varnothing , we select the nearest member to p 0 p_{0} , breaking distance ties by a larger observed window margin and then a deterministic coordinate order. If 𝒞 = ∅ \mathcal{C}=\varnothing , selection over 𝒢 \mathcal{G} prioritizes margin, local qualified density, and adjustment distance, and records that no fully supported interior target exists. The margin is the L ∞ L_{\infty} distance to the boundary of the union of known qualified cells, measured in grid units. The selected point p ⋆ p^{\star} supplies an existing image I g = I ⁡ ( p ⋆ ) I_{g}=I(p^{\star}) . Interpolation constructs correction labels only; current and reference SEMs are measured. The imitation target follows straight-line interpolation: a k ⋆ \displaystyle a_{k}^{\star} = p ⋆ − p 0 H , k = 0 , … , H − 2 , \displaystyle=\frac{p^{\star}-p_{0}}{H},\quad k=0,\ldots,H-2, (3) a H − 1 ⋆ \displaystyle a_{H-1}^{\star} = p ⋆ − p 0 − ∑ k = 0 H − 2 a k ⋆ . \displaystyle=p^{\star}-p_{0}-\sum_{k=0}^{H-2}a_{k}^{\star}. The final residual corrects numerical accumulation. These increments encode an endpoint plan; no intermediate observation or action duration is available. Target construction changes both the reference appearance and action supervision. Its ablation must therefore be interpreted as a change in the complete target-construction policy. We retain two subsets: SEM-73 (73 workbooks, 4,334 measured points) and SEM-100 (100 groups, 9,900 measured points), totaling 14,234 points. Their training/validation/test recovery-pair counts are 413/202/200 and 4,514/628/1,363, respectively; FEM-group splits are 51/11/11 and 70/10/20. Eight SEM-73 test morphology groups contain recovery pairs. Grouping uses image hashes and morphology; wafer/lot metadata are unavailable. All 2,915 missing SEM-73 grid locations remain unknown. Interior targets exist for 754/815 SEM-73 and 5,521/6,505 SEM-100 pairs. Qualified-region success (GSR) accepts any known qualified endpoint.

Interior success (ISR) uses all pairs as its denominator; interior availability is 100% for SEM-73 test pairs and approximately 81.36% for SEM-100 pairs. Macro-GSR weights evaluated groups equally. These curated successes use FEM lookup, not newly acquired closed-loop observations; SEM-73 GSR is 89.0%. 4.2 Training and comparison protocol LithoWorld is trained on our merged FEM training split using two NVIDIA H200 GPUs. It uses global batch 256 with equal subset sampling, AdamW for 40,000 updates, peak learning rate × 10 − 4 2\!\times\!10^{-4} , 1,200 warmup updates, cosine decay to 10 − 5 10^{-5} , zero weight decay, and gradient clipping at 1.0. BF16 autocast retains FP32 parameters and optimizer states. LoRA rank/scale/dropout are 32/64/0.1; DINOv2 remains frozen in evaluation mode. The 16-layer flow head has 32 attention heads of width 48; its internal attention width is 1,536, distinct from the configured hidden width of 1,024. All comparison methods are trained or fine-tuned on the FEM training split and evaluated on the same test split. Table 1 reports a common frozen-DINOv2 comparison with identical input SEMs, reference selection, parameter normalization, splits, and evaluator. DINOv2+MLP predicts the total correction directly. ACT-goal and Diffusion Policy-goal add reference conditioning.

MDT-image uses image goals and disables unavailable language and intermediate-frame objectives; ManiFlow-goal retains consistency flow training; MoDE-goal retains expert routing. All use two-dimensional actions, with horizon eight except the explicit direct-output control. Thus, the names denote adaptations trained for our task. Tables report the mean and sample standard deviation over three runs. Each method produces one candidate per input, and the evaluator scores its endpoint without test-label reranking. The checkpoint used for qualitative analysis is identified separately so that single-run case statistics are not conflated with the aggregate comparison. The test split was monitored during development; evaluation on independent batches remains an important next step. 4.3 Comparative results and ablations LithoWorld achieves 88.5% SEM-73 GSR in Table 1 , compared with 86.0% for ManiFlow-goal and 80.0% for direct regression. Its 46.0% ISR exceeds ManiFlow-goal by 6.0 points, while mean margin rises from 0.78 to 0.94 grid units. Thus, the gain extends beyond reaching a qualified cell to obtaining stronger local window support. Removing endpoint alignment lowers GSR by 3.0 points and ISR by 4.5 points. On SEM-100, LithoWorld attains 86.0% GSR, slightly below ManiFlow-goal at 86.4%, but improves ISR from 31.6% to 32.5%. 4.4 Observed results and SEM recovery cases The checkpoint-15,000 archive provides SEM-73 GSR of 89.0% (178/200), ISR of 43.0% (86/200), macro-GSR of 93.75%, and mean margin of 0.9244 grid units. SEM-100 yields 86.57% GSR and 28.32% ISR. These statistics describe the checkpoint used in Fig. 2 ; Table 1 reports the separate three-run aggregate. SEM-73 failures are unevenly distributed: one 48-pair group accounts for 21 of 22 failures. The higher macro score therefore does not imply uniform reliability. Across monitored checkpoints, SEM-73 GSR peaks at 89.5% at update 22,500, while ISR peaks at 54.5% at update 7,500; qualification and interior placement favor different checkpoints. Figure 2 shows two morphologically different SEM-73 cases from the fixed 15,000-update archive. Eight predicted increments are accumulated without resampling or replanning. Each displayed SEM is retrieved from the same FEM at q = ⌊ p + 0.5 ⌋ q=\lfloor p+0.5\rfloor on each grid axis. The line-pattern case first matches a qualified cell at S7; the branched-pattern case does so at S4. Both final cells are interior, with observed margins of 1.0891 and 1.7190 grid units. In (b), the endpoint cell ( 4 , 4 ) (4,4) differs from the reference cell ( 5 , 4 ) (5,4) , illustrating process-window recovery without exact target-coordinate matching. They were selected from successful cases and do not establish monotonic defect reduction or population performance. 4.5 Scope The world model regularizes endpoint representations; it lacks action-conditioned intermediate SEM supervision. Grid axes have no physical dose/focus calibration, and lookup images are not measurements newly acquired at the continuous predictions. Deployment also requires a practical source of the qualified reference. If historical qualified coordinates are available, direct reuse of those coordinates is an additional baseline.

Independent batches, calibrated process axes, and group-level uncertainty estimates are needed to assess transfer beyond this offline benchmark. Concentrated SEM-73 failures motivate reporting both pair-weighted and group-weighted scores: strong performance on small groups can obscure failures on a frequent morphology. Macro-GSR should therefore accompany GSR and per-group counts. ISR tests discrete core membership, whereas margin measures clearance within the qualified-cell union. These complementary metrics distinguish qualification, interior placement, and morphological variation, but neither certifies tolerance to unmeasured physical perturbations. 4.1 FEM dataset and evaluation All 173 FEM groups contain acquired SEMs, with no simulated or generated images. They were selected from successful cases and do not establish monotonic defect reduction or population performance. 5 Conclusion LithoWorld connects endpoint world modeling with lithography process-window recovery through shared interior targets. Its direct policy learns SEM-conditioned corrections while evaluation accepts any observed qualified endpoint. On the SEM-73 test pairs, it achieves 88.5% qualified-region success and 46.0% interior success. The ablations show complementary benefits from interior target selection and endpoint alignment, while the direct-output control clarifies the role of action chunking. Future work will examine calibrated process coordinates and feedback from newly acquired SEMs.
